hot.pointer_line: On now: the Suquet de Peix fish-stew days in Roses until Sunday 25 October, clocks back on 25 October, the castanyada for Tots Sants on 1 November, the olive harvest at the Empordà mills and the MICHELIN Spain 2027 gala in Huesca on 24 November; the Festa de l'Anxova (4 October) and the 2026 music festival (ended 21 August) are over, the sea is cooling from about 19C and the tramuntana season is back.

groups.title: In the water
groups.desc: The bathing season is over in all but name: the sea is cooling, the tramuntana is coming back and the urchins are on their way.

items.name: The sea in late October
items.teaser: October water at Cadaqués averages about 19C and drops through the month; a swim only on calm days
items.story: The honest number: the long-run October average for the sea at Cadaqués is about 19.1C, with a spread from roughly 16.7C to 21.9C depending on the year and the wind. The climate tables call it a fresh swim, not a pleasant one, and the bay cools week by week into November. The tramuntana makes it worse: a day of north wind stirs the water and chills the coves on the exposed side of the cape. Calm, sunny afternoons in the sheltered bays of the village and Portlligat are the window. From Sunday 25 October the clocks go back and the light goes earlier.
items.why: Swim after two calm days, at midday, in the bay rather than out on the cape.
facts: Mid-Oct to end Nov, cooling week by week
These are long-run averages, not today's reading: put a hand in before you commit

items.name: The tramuntana season returns
items.teaser: The north wind is back for the winter half of the year: gusts past 100 km/h close the cape and the boats
items.story: Autumn is when the tramuntana takes the cape back. It is the cold, dry wind that pours down from the Pyrenees, and in a strong episode the Alt Empordà gets Meteocat's warnings first: a red warning in late March 2026 covered the comarca, and the highest gusts in a Girona-wide blow are routinely logged at Portbou, just up the coast, at over 130 km/h. On those days the Generalitat has closed access to the Cap de Creus Natural Park as a precaution and small boats stay in. The reward follows: scoured, glassy light over the white houses once it drops.
items.why: Read the Meteocat marine forecast the night before any boat or cape day; keep the old town and a long lunch as the fallback.
facts: Episodes any time from now through spring
The whole Cap de Creus peninsula

items.name: The sea-urchin season is coming
items.teaser: Garotes are a December-to-March food: the legal season and the urchin menus are still ahead
items.story: The violet urchins on the Cadaqués schist are eaten in the cold months, when the roe is full; the guide's kitchens serve them from roughly December to March. Gathering is regulated: Catalonia's Ordre ARP/105/2020 set a management plan for professional urchin gatherers and a closed season for recreational catches, and the Catalan press has reported the recreational daily limit being halved from 150 to 75 pieces. The exact 2026-27 opening date was not found online. The best-known restaurant campaign, La Garoinada in Palafrugell, ran 16 January to 29 March in 2026.
items.why: Do not expect urchins on the menu before December; ask, and accept a no.
facts: Expected from about December; 2026-27 opening date not confirmed

items.name: Cap de Creus without the summer controls
items.teaser: The lighthouse road is regulated in summer only; in autumn the cape is open, quiet and walkable
items.story: In summer the Parc Natural limits private cars on the road from Cadaqués to the lighthouse: in its 2024 calendar the restriction ran every day in June, July, August and September, from 9:30 to 21:30, with a shuttle from the free Corral d'en Morell car park. The 2026 calendar was not found online, but the regulation is a summer measure and October is outside it. Walking access has never been restricted: the old lighthouse path and the GR11 are always open. Autumn is the season for the cape itself, the twisted schist of Paratge de Tudela and Cala Culip below the lighthouse, with almost nobody on them.
items.why: Go on a still day: in a tramuntana the headland is unwalkable and access can be closed.
facts: Open now; summer road controls ran June-September in 2024 (2026 dates not found)

items.name: The olive harvest and the new oil
items.teaser: Argudell and Corivell olives go to the Empordà mills now; Spain expects a harvest 23% up on last year
items.story: Late autumn is olive time in the Empordà, and the oil is DOP Oli de l'Empordà, made from the two native varieties, Argudell and Corivell. The nearest working cooperative is Empordàlia at Pau, inland from Roses, formed in 2005 from the Pau-Roses and Vilajuïga co-ops; its Oli de Pau comes from centenarian trees. Nationally, the first estimates presented on 1 October 2026 point to 1.6 million tonnes, 23% more than last year, after a wet spring. No date for the 2026 Empordà new-oil presentation was found. The Ventalló oil fair was on 27 September; Espolla's comes in January.
items.why: Ask at the cooperative shop whether the oli nou is in yet: the first green, peppery oil is the reason to go.
facts: Harvest under way through late autumn; new-oil date not announced

items.story: The Casa Salvador Dalí at Portlligat, the fishermen's huts Dalí and Gala joined into a house over forty years, is visited only by timed, pre-booked slot in small groups. The foundation's 2026 calendar was not found in search; in 2025 the house opened 10:30 to 17:10 outside the summer, closed some Mondays, and shut entirely from 7 January to 10 February. Online tickets were 15 EUR in 2025. Autumn is the easiest time to get a slot, and the low light on the bay matches the window Dalí painted from.

items.name: Suquet de Peix days in Roses: 16-25 October
items.teaser: Thirteen Roses restaurants put their own suquet de peix on a menu until Sunday 25 October, 30-70 EUR
items.story: The suquet is the fishermen's stew of the Costa Brava: rock fish and potatoes simmered in a sofregit and finished with a picada of garlic, almonds and saffron. Every autumn the Ajuntament de Roses gives it ten days, and in 2026 the Jornades Gastronòmiques del Suquet de Peix run from 16 to 25 October, with menus from 30 to 70 EUR. The participating list includes El Trull, Rafa's, Cal Negre, Bitakora, Hostal Risech, Sodemar, Ca la Valeria, Roc-Fort, L'Àncora, Falconera, El Mirador de l'Almadrava, La Cala and Tramonti Platja. Roses is the next town south, over the Pení.
items.why: Book the weekend lunches: the menus are a set price and fill with locals.
facts: Menus are published on the Visit Roses event page

items.name: Castanyada: chestnuts and panellets for Tots Sants
items.teaser: For All Saints, Catalonia roasts chestnuts and eats panellets, the pine-nut marzipan balls, with sweet wine
items.story: Tots Sants, 1 November, is a public holiday in Spain, and in Catalonia the night before belongs to the castanyada, a custom with more than three centuries behind it. Chestnut sellers appear in the streets and markets a few days before; at home the table holds roasted chestnuts, roasted sweet potatoes and panellets, the small balls of almond marzipan rolled in pine nuts. The origin is argued over: one account ties it to bell-ringers eating chestnuts on All Saints' night, another links panellets to offerings for the dead. Any village pastry shop will have trays of them that week.
items.why: Buy panellets from a pastry shop, not a supermarket, and drink a glass of moscatell with them.
facts: Pastry shops and streets across Catalonia

items.name: Festa de l'Anxova, L'Escala: over for 2026
items.teaser: The 36th anchovy feast was on 4 October and the tapa route ended on the 11th; the salters stay open
items.story: The anchovy town down the coast had its day on Sunday 4 October 2026: the 36th Festa de l'Anxova, with the pregó and the Anxova d'Or presented at La Punta at noon, a popular tasting on La Riba and havaneres on the beach. The Ruta de la Tapa de l'Anxova ran in the bars from 2 to 11 October at 3 EUR a tapa. Both are over. The reason to go remains: L'Escala's salters cure the anchovies in salt for months and fillet them by hand, and their shops sell them all year.
items.why: Too late for the feast: go for a tin of filets from a salting house instead.

items.name: Clocks go back: Sunday 25 October
items.teaser: Summer time ends at 3:00 on Sunday 25 October: sunset comes an hour earlier by the clock
items.story: Spain, like the rest of the EU, leaves summer time on the last Sunday of October: in 2026 that is Sunday 25 October, when 3:00 becomes 2:00. For anyone working the boat or the kitchen it changes the shape of the day: an hour more light in the morning for the market and the fish, an hour less after a late lunch, and the long golden evenings on the bay are over. Plan cape walks and boat runs for the middle of the day and get back before dusk.
items.why: Move the long lunch earlier and keep the afternoon walk short.
facts: Check that the boat's and the crew's devices updated

items.name: MICHELIN Spain 2027 gala: Tuesday 24 November, Huesca
items.teaser: The 2027 stars for Spain are announced in Huesca on 24 November; Compartir Cadaqués will be watching
items.story: The MICHELIN Guide Spain 2027 ceremony will be held on Tuesday 24 November 2026 at the Palacio de Congresos de Huesca, in the Auditorio Carlos Saura, the first time the gala goes to Aragon. Carmelo Bosque, chef of the one-star Lillas Pastia in Huesca, is in charge of the dinner. For Cadaqués the result to watch is Compartir, the village's MICHELIN-listed table, run by the Disfrutar trio. Results are published the same evening.
items.why: Book Compartir before the gala, not after: a new distinction fills a book overnight.

items.story: The Festival Internacional de Música de Cadaqués, born in Santa Maria in 1970, changed its shape in 2026: the 53rd edition ran from 28 June to 21 August, opening with Handel's Messiah with the BCN City Ballet and the Orquestra Filharmònica del Mediterrani, and including Brahms's German Requiem with the Orfeó Gracienc on 24 July. items.name: Festivitat de Sant Sebastià
items.teaser: Bells, a climb to the hermitage on the Pení slopes, Mass, sardanes and patacades: the village's January feast
items.story: Every 20 January Cadaqués walks up to the hermitage of Sant Sebastià. In 2026 the Ajuntament's programme opened with bell-ringing and the ascent at 9:30, Mass at 11:00 and sardanes at the hermitage, then patacades, songs and dances, at 15:00, more sardanes at Es Portal at 16:30, hot chocolate at the Casal de la Gent Gran at 17:00 and an evening concert in the Plaça de Ses Herbes at 18:30. It is the village's day, not a show for visitors, and the hermitage looks down on the whole bay.
items.why: Walk up with the village in the morning; the view from the hermitage is the point.
facts: 20 January every year (Wed 20 Jan 2027; programme not yet published)

items.name: La Garoinada of Palafrugell
items.teaser: Restaurants of Palafrugell, Llafranc and Calella cook the urchin through the January lows until Easter
items.story: The coast's best-known urchin campaign runs in Palafrugell and its two sea villages, Llafranc and Calella de Palafrugell, where the urchin is called garoina. In 2026 La Garoinada ran from 16 January to 29 March with nine restaurants and six hotels; in 2025 it ran 17 January to 31 March. The season follows the January minves, the calm low tides, and its end moves with Easter. In Cadaqués the same urchin, called garota here, is served in the cold months by kitchens such as La Sirena.
items.why: Eat them raw with bread first, then try them in eggs.
facts: Usually mid-January to late March; 2027 dates not yet published

items.teaser: The winter festa of the Mare de Déu de l'Esperança: a solemn Mass, sardanes at Es Portal, four days
items.story: Cadaqués keeps two festes majors, and the winter one belongs to the village. It is built around the feast of the Mare de Déu de l'Esperança on 18 December: in 2025 it ran from 18 to 21 December, with a solemn Mass in the church on the 18th and sardanes at Es Portal, then magic and concerts, a tennis tournament, a butifarra card tournament, a popular lunch and a dance through the weekend. In 2024 it ran 13 to 18 December. It is the last big date before the Dalí house closes for the winter.
items.why: Stay for the sardanes at Es Portal after the Mass.

items.story: Born in the church of Santa Maria in 1970, the festival is the village's summer institution, though its calendar moves. items.name: Sant Pere, the fishermen's saint
items.teaser: 29 June belongs to Saint Peter, patron of fishermen, in every Catalan port that still has boats
items.story: Sant Pere, on 29 June, is the fishermen's feast along the Catalan coast: in the old fishing quarters it means processions to the beach, the blessing of the boats, havaneres and rom cremat after dark. The guide's earlier research listed it as the fishermen's day in Cadaqués too. A current Cadaqués programme was not found online, so treat the day as a date to ask about in the village rather than a fixed show: the harbour and the Confraria are where it happens.
items.why: Ask at the harbour in late June what is planned for the 29th.
facts: 29 June every year; Cadaqués programme not found

items.name: Cantada d'Havaneres, Calella de Palafrugell
items.teaser: Sea songs from Cuba and cremat on the Port Bo beach, first Saturday of July; 2026 was cancelled for a fire
items.story: The great night of havaneres, the songs Catalan sailors brought back from the Cuba trade, is held on the first Saturday of July on the Port Bo of Calella de Palafrugell, with cremat burning blue in the dark. It has been sung for sixty years. The 2026 edition, set for Saturday 4 July, was cancelled that afternoon on the orders of Protecció Civil because of a fire, and the return of the song El meu avi to the official repertoire was put off a year. The 2027 date has not been announced.
items.why: Arrive in the afternoon for a place on the sand.
facts: Usually first Saturday of July; 2027 date not yet announced

items.name: Festa Major d'Estiu
items.teaser: A week of harbour swims, sea cucanyes, giants, havaneres and sardanes; 4-11 September in 2026
items.story: The summer festa major fills the second week of September. In 2026 it ran from 4 to 11 September: a Friday of children's games, a foam party, havaneres at 22:00 and a midnight dance; a Saturday of popular swims across the harbour, sea cucanyes on the greasy pole, giants and a tug of war; and a Sunday with the festa major Mass, a simultaneous chess match and sardanes at 19:00. It is the village at its most itself, with the summer crowd thinning out.
items.why: Watch the harbour swims and cucanyes on the Saturday from the waterfront.

items.name: The verema in the DO Empordà
items.teaser: Grapes come in from late August through September; 2026 was a hot, early year across Catalonia
items.story: Harvest in the Empordà runs from late summer into the start of autumn, on the slopes behind the coast. In 2026 heat and little rain pushed Catalonia's harvest early: in the DO Penedès most growers started picking before August, the earliest on record, with healthy but light fruit. No harvest balance for the DO Empordà was found by mid-October. Cooperatives such as Empordàlia at Pau, which make wine as well as oil, are the easy place to taste the new vintage.
items.why: Visit a cellar in October, when the wine is in the tanks and the rush is over.
facts: Usually late August to early October
